thread:
Evelyn Park: quick design check: thinking about sharding policy bundles by tenant and adding gateway prefetch heuristics. idea: gateway subscribes to bundle shards for tenants it serves and keeps an LRU of recently used RID -> policy blobs. tradeoffs?
Omar Said: sounds promising. shards reduce bundle size per gateway. concern: tenant hot-switching (many tenants on same gateway) could trash cache. need prefetch heuristics + eviction policy.
Priya Patel: ops note: for hosted customers with many small projects, prefetch could blow memory. maybe use a lightweight heatmap service: gateway reports recent tenant hits and control plane pushes top-N shards proactively.
Liam O'Connor: +1 for heatmap. also consider short-lived per-request lookups for cold tenants: gateway queries a shard lookup endpoint (fast path) and caches result with tiny TTL. prefer cache fills to full remote RBAC eval.
Evelyn Park: what about revocation semantics across shards? if we remove a role membership, gateways must see tombstones. propose tombstone vector per-rid with sequence number; token carries seq number so gateway can detect stale local state and trigger shard refresh.
Omar Said: seq numbers are good. also add a small failure mode: if seq mismatch and shard unavailable, gate fallback should be deny-by-default for sensitive routes and allow-with-flag for low-risk ones. document per-route policy.
Priya Patel: migration: legacy API keys -> broker mints ephemeral runtime token with rid + seq. we can A/B canary by enabling shard-prefetch for 10% of traffic and measure memory/latency.
Liam O'Connor: perf targets: session-cache hit p99 < 8ms. prefetch should aim to keep miss rate < 5% for top tenants. I'll prototype a heatmap + prefetch sim.
sec-bot: added runbook entry: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/policy-sharding (task: "shard-prefetch-canary")
Evelyn Park: action items: Omar draft shard API + tombstone seq scheme, Priya write canary plan & risk matrix, Liam bench heatmap prefetch. reconvene Tue 11am to fold into RFC.
